title: Tax is charged on the undiscounted subtotal, so discounted orders are overcharged
summary: For orders at or above 1,000.00 the 10% tax is calculated on the full subtotal instead of the subtotal after the 5% discount, so every discounted order total is too high.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
POST /api/orders with 100 x p-101 and 100 x p-104 (subtotal 1,000.00, exactly at the threshold), see evidence for the exact request
Read tax_cents and total_cents
Repeat in Client Portal > New order with 12 x Printer Toner Cartridge: the confirmation shows $1,133.88
expected: Subtotal 100000, discount 5000, tax 9500 (10% of 95000), total 104500. For 12 toners: tax 10259, total 112848.
actual: Tax 10000 and total 105000 at the threshold; tax 10799 and total 113388 ($1,133.88) for 12 toners. Order detail and admin Reports totals inherit the wrong figure.
suspected_cause: src/pricing.mjs computes tax from subtotal rather than subtotal minus discount

regression_test.description: Price an order with subtotal 100000 and expect tax 9500 and total 104500

title: Any signed-in client can read another company's order by id
summary: GET /api/orders/{id} does not check which company owns the order, so a client from one company can read another company's order.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 and POST /api/orders (reference QA-T01), note the id
Sign in as bright-1 and GET /api/orders/{id}
Repeat as zain-1
expected: HTTP 403 or 404 for a different company
actual: HTTP 200 with the full order (items, prices, totals) for both bright-1 and zain-1
suspected_cause: getOrder looks the order up by id only and never compares client_id to the caller

regression_test.description: Client B requests client A's order id and expects 404

title: Clients can list all customers, including personal and payment details
summary: GET /api/admin/customers has no admin-only check: any signed-in client receives every company's customer records, which contain personal contact data and card details.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
GET /api/admin/customers
Repeat as bright-1
actual: HTTP 200 with all customers from all companies (contact names, phone numbers, national IDs, addresses, card fragments and notes)
suspected_cause: Route is declared without roles: ['admin'] in src/api.mjs

title: A session token keeps working after sign-out
summary: POST /api/auth/logout returns 204 but the same token is still accepted afterwards.
steps: Sign in over the API as zain-1
POST /api/auth/logout (204)
GET /api/me with the same token
GET /api/orders with the same token
actual: HTTP 200 on both calls; the data is still readable. The Client Portal Sign out button only returns to the sign-in page.
suspected_cause: Logout only sets endedAt on the session; authenticate() never checks endedAt or expiresAt

regression_test.description: Logout, then GET /me with the same token and expect 401

title: Orders accept quantity 0, negative, above 1000 and fractional values, and orders with no items
summary: The order endpoint only checks that quantity is a number; the documented 1 to 1,000 whole-number rule and the at-least-one-item rule are not enforced.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
POST /api/orders with quantity -3 (and separately 0, 1001, 2.5)
POST /api/orders with items: []
expected: HTTP 400 for each (quantity must be a whole number from 1 to 1000; at least one item)
actual: HTTP 201 each time; a negative quantity creates a negative-value order, and an empty order is created
suspected_cause: validateOrderInput in src/api.mjs checks typeof quantity only and does not check items.length

regression_test.description: POST orders with quantity -3, 0, 1001, 1.5 and empty items; expect 400 each

title: Client order list shows stale status after an admin changes it
summary: My Orders (and the status filter) is served from a 10-minute per-company cache, so a status change made by an admin is not shown in the list although the order detail shows it.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal as acme-1 and open My orders (warms the list)
In the Admin Portal open order QA-UI-1 and click Update status to Processing
Sign in to the Client Portal as acme-2 and open My orders
Open order QA-UI-1 detail, then reload My orders
expected: List and detail both show Processing
actual: Detail shows Processing, list still shows Placed (and GET /api/orders?status=processing does not return the changed order)
suspected_cause: listClientOrders caches copies of orders for 10 minutes and status updates do not invalidate them

regression_test.description: Warm client list, change status as admin, re-read list and expect new status

title: Double-clicking Place order creates duplicate orders
summary: The Place order button is not disabled after the first click and the API has no duplicate protection, so a double click creates two identical orders. I am not sure the product intends to block duplicates, but a customer would be charged twice for one intent.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal as acme-1
Open New order: reference QA-UI-2, product Staples box of 5000, quantity 1
Double-click Place order
Open My orders
actual: Two orders QA-UI-2 appear (two QA-UI-1 also appeared with the toner order); POST /api/orders sent twice at once returns 201 for both
suspected_cause: No in-flight guard on the submit button and no idempotency key

regression_test.description: Double-click submit and expect a single order in the list

title: Order list search with a regex character (for example '(') returns a server error
summary: The q parameter is compiled as a regular expression, so invalid patterns crash with HTTP 500.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
GET /api/orders?q=(
GET /api/orders?q=\
expected: Literal text search; HTTP 200 with no matches
suspected_cause: new RegExp(q) in listOrders; should escape the text or use includes()

title: page_size=0 causes HTTP 500 and negative page_size is accepted
summary: page_size is only checked against the upper bound of 100. Zero crashes the request and negative values return 200 with a negative page_size.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
GET /api/orders?page_size=0
GET /api/orders?page_size=-5
expected: HTTP 400: page_size must be between 1 and 100

title: Malformed JSON responses expose a stack trace and server file paths
summary: Sending a malformed JSON body returns 400 with a stack trace and source paths in the body.
steps: POST /api/auth/login with a body that is not valid JSON
POST /api/orders as acme-1 with a malformed body
expected: A short error message with no internals
actual: Body contains a stack field with server file paths
suspected_cause: The body parser error includes err.stack in the response

regression_test.description: Malformed JSON returns 400 with no stack field

title: On mobile, the My orders toolbar covers the top of the table and the Total and View columns are cut off
summary: At 390px wide the table starts underneath the status filter toolbar, hiding the column headers and the first row, and Total and View sit outside the visible width with no cue.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal as acme-1
Set the viewport to 390x844
Open My orders
expected: Table starts below the toolbar and key columns are reachable
actual: Table top (199px) is behind the toolbar (bottom 263px); the table is 450px wide inside a 359px box

regression_test.description: Check toolbar bottom is at or above table top at 390px

title: Several controls have no accessible name
summary: The product select on New order, the Admin Orders search box (placeholder only) and the two icon buttons beside the status filter (refresh, clear filters) have no accessible name.
steps: Open Client Portal > New order and run the page audit
Open Admin Portal > Orders and run the page audit
actual: Audit lists select[name=product], input#search, button#refresh and button#clear-filters as unnamed

regression_test.description: Assert each form control has an accessible name

title: Sales report takes about 4 seconds and shows only a spinner
summary: GET /api/admin/reports/sales took over 4 seconds in both runs; the page shows a spinner with no text meanwhile.
steps: Sign in to the Admin Portal
Open Reports and watch the page for 4 seconds
expected: Report within about 3 seconds, or a loading message
suspected_cause: Deliberate latency or slow aggregation in salesReport
